legend: Bessie is trying to convert a number X$$$X$$$ to Y$$$Y$$$.

In one operation, Bessie can choose an integer M$$$M$$$ (M≥1$$$M \ge 1$$$) and round X$$$X$$$ to the nearest multiple of M$$$M$$$. If X$$$X$$$ is exactly in the middle of two multiples of M$$$M$$$, it is rounded up. Note that 0$$$0$$$ is a multiple of every number.
What is the least number of operations Bessie needs to perform to convert X$$$X$$$ to Y$$$Y$$$? Output this number, or −1$$$-1$$$ if it is impossible.
input: The first line contains a single integer T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤104$$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
Each of the next T$$$T$$$ lines contains two integers X$$$X$$$ and Y$$$Y$$$ (1≤X,Y≤109$$$1 \le X, Y \le 10^9$$$) — the initial number and the target number.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations required, or −1$$$-1$$$ if it is impossible.
note: In the first testcase of the first sample, X=2$$$X=2$$$ and Y=5$$$Y=5$$$. Bessie can perform the following 2$$$2$$$ operations:
Choose M=4$$$M=4$$$. The multiples of 4$$$4$$$ are 0,4,8,…$$$0, 4, 8, \dots$$$. X=2$$$X=2$$$ is exactly in the middle of 0$$$0$$$ and 4$$$4$$$, so it rounds up to 4$$$4$$$. Now X=4$$$X=4$$$.
Choose M=5$$$M=5$$$. The multiples of 5$$$5$$$ are 0,5,10,…$$$0, 5, 10, \dots$$$. The nearest multiple to 4$$$4$$$ is 5$$$5$$$. Now X=5$$$X=5$$$.
It can be proven that it is impossible to do this in fewer than 2$$$2$$$ operations.
In the second testcase of the first sample, X=6$$$X=6$$$ and Y=4$$$Y=4$$$.
It can be proven that it is impossible to do this in fewer than 2$$$2$$$ operations.
